title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 20.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 20, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The children of Moab and Ammon come against Jehoshaphat to battle
Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast throughout all Judah
Jehoshaphat stands in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of the LORD
Judah gathers together to seek help from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Moab and Ammon come against Jehoshaphat to battle
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:1 states that after this, the children of Moab and Ammon came against Jehoshaphat to battle, which is the first event mentioned.

questions.question: Who came against Jehoshaphat to battle according to 2 Chronicles 20?
options: Children of Moab and Ammon with others
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Moab and Ammon with others
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:1 states that the children of Moab, the children of Ammon, and others beside the Ammonites came against Jehoshaphat to battle.

questions.question: Where were the great multitude that came against Jehoshaphat found according to the report?
options: Beyond the sea on the other side of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Hazazontamar, which is Engedi
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:2 reports that the great multitude was found in Hazazontamar, which is Engedi.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do when he feared the coming multitude?
options: He set himself to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah
He immediately went out to battle
questions.correctAnswer: He set himself to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:3 says that Jehoshaphat feared and set himself to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

questions.question: From where did the people of Judah gather to ask for help from the LORD?
options: From all the cities of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: From all the cities of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:4 states that Judah gathered themselves together even out of all the cities of Judah to seek the LORD.

questions.question: Where did Jehoshaphat stand to speak to the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem?
options: In the house of the LORD, before the new court
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of the LORD, before the new court
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:5 says that Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court.

questions.question: How does Jehoshaphat address God in his prayer regarding God's power?
options: O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen?
O LORD, why have you forsaken us?
God of Israel, why do you not protect us?
Almighty God, please fight for us
questions.correctAnswer: O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:6 contains Jehoshaphat's prayer stating, 'O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen?'

questions.question: Who does Jehoshaphat say God gave the land to, as mentioned in his prayer?
options: The seed of Abraham thy friend forever
questions.correctAnswer: The seed of Abraham thy friend forever
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:7 states that God gave the land to the seed of Abraham his friend forever.

questions.question: What did God's people build in the land He gave them, according to Jehoshaphat's prayer?
questions.correctAnswer: A sanctuary for God's name
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:8 says they dwelt therein and built a sanctuary for God's name.

questions.question: According to Jehoshaphat's prayer, what will God do if they stand before the house and cry unto Him in affliction?
questions.correctAnswer: He will hear and help
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:9 states that if they stand before the house and cry unto God in affliction, He will hear and help.

questions.question: Which people did God not allow Israel to invade when they came out of Egypt, as mentioned by Jehoshaphat?
options: Children of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:10 explains that God would not let Israel invade the children of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir when they came out of Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: All Judah stood before the LORD with their little ones, wives, and children.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:13 states that all Judah stood before the LORD with their little ones, wives, and children.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat and the people of Judah proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah when they sought the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:3 states that Jehoshaphat proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat said that God had sent many prophets to warn them about the coming battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text in 2 Chronicles 20 does not mention Jehoshaphat saying anything about God sending many prophets to warn them.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat expressed confidence that they had the might to defeat the great company coming against them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:12 says they had no might against the great company and did not know what to do, but their eyes were upon God.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was filled with the Spirit of the LORD in the midst of the congregation?
options: A Levite of the children of Kohath
questions.correctAnswer: Jahaziel the son of Zechariah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:14 states that the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah in the midst of the congregation.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 20:17 promise will happen if the people 'stand ye still and see the salvation of the LORD' as commanded in 2 Chronicles 20:16?
options: They shall see the salvation of the LORD with them
They will be defeated by the enemy
They must fight hard to win
questions.correctAnswer: They shall see the salvation of the LORD with them
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:17 promises that the people shall see the salvation of the LORD with them if they stand still as instructed in 2 Chronicles 20:16.

questions.question: What specific instruction did Jahaziel give regarding fighting in the battle?
options: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle
Use weapons of war to defend yourselves
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:17 clearly states that they shall not need to fight in this battle and should stand still to see the LORD's salvation.

questions.question: How did Jehoshaphat and the people respond immediately after hearing Jahaziel's prophecy about God's deliverance?
options: They bowed their heads and worshipped the LORD
They prepared for battle with weapons
They fled the city in fear
questions.correctAnswer: They bowed their heads and worshipped the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:18 states that Jehoshaphat bowed his head to the ground and all Judah and Jerusalem worshipped the LORD after hearing the prophecy.

questions.question: What role did the Levites play after Jehoshaphat’s prayer and prophecy?
options: They praised the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice
They went out to fight the enemy
They remained silent and prayed individually
questions.correctAnswer: They praised the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:19 records that the Levites stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice.

questions.question: What two things did Jehoshaphat urge the people to do in 2 Chronicles 20:20 before going out to battle?
options: Believe in the LORD your God and believe his prophets
Gather weapons and fortify the city
Fast and weep before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Believe in the LORD your God and believe his prophets
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:20 shows Jehoshaphat encouraging the people to believe in the LORD and in His prophets for their establishment and prosperity.

questions.question: What unique strategy did Jehoshaphat implement as the army went out to battle?
options: He appointed singers to praise the LORD before the army
He sent spies to scout the enemy
He divided the army into three groups
questions.correctAnswer: He appointed singers to praise the LORD before the army
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:21 states that Jehoshaphat appointed singers to go before the army praising the LORD.

questions.question: What happened when the singers began to praise the LORD?
options: The LORD set ambushments against the enemy
The earth shook and the battle was delayed
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD set ambushments against the enemy
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:22 explains that when the singers praised the LORD, He set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab and mount Seir, leading to their defeat.

questions.question: How did the enemy groups end up fighting each other?
options: The children of Ammon and Moab turned against the inhabitants of mount Seir
They united to fight against Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Ammon and Moab turned against the inhabitants of mount Seir
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:23 states that the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir and destroyed them, then each group helped destroy another.

questions.question: What did Judah find when they approached the watch tower in the wilderness?
options: Dead bodies fallen to the earth, none escaped
questions.correctAnswer: Dead bodies fallen to the earth, none escaped
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:24 describes how Judah saw the multitude of dead bodies when they approached the watch tower, with none escaping.

questions.question: How long did it take the people of Judah to gather the spoils from the defeated enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:25 mentions that they spent three days gathering the abundant spoil from the dead bodies.

questions.question: Why was the valley where Judah assembled on the fourth day called the Valley of Berachah?
options: Because they blessed the LORD there
Because it was a place of battle
Because it was a place of fasting
Because it was a location of mourning
questions.correctAnswer: Because they blessed the LORD there
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:26 states they assembled in the valley to bless the LORD, hence the name 'The valley of Berachah' meaning blessing.

questions.question: The people of Judah responded to the LORD's prophecy by worshipping and praising Him before the battle began.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:18-19 records that Jehoshaphat and the people worshipped and the Levites praised the LORD before going to battle.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat told the people to prepare weapons and fight hard, as the battle was theirs to win by their own strength.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:15 says the battle is not theirs but God's, and 20:17 says they shall not need to fight, indicating reliance on God, not their own strength.

questions.question: The battle ended with Judah suffering heavy losses and retreating back to Jerusalem in defeat.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:24-26 describes Judah finding the enemy dead with none escaping and gathering great spoil, indicating a victorious outcome.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 20.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 20:27, who led the people of Judah and Jerusalem back to Jerusalem with joy after their victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:27 states that Jehoshaphat was in the forefront of them returning to Jerusalem with joy.

questions.question: What musical instruments are mentioned in 2 Chronicles 20:28 as being brought to the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalteries, harps, and trumpets
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:28 specifically lists psalteries, harps, and trumpets brought to the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What effect did the LORD's victory have on the surrounding kingdoms as described in 2 Chronicles 20:29?
options: Fear of God fell on all the kingdoms
They sought an alliance with Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of God fell on all the kingdoms
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:29 says the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of those countries when they heard the LORD fought against Israel's enemies.

questions.question: How long did Jehoshaphat reign over Judah according to 2 Chronicles 20:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty and five years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:31 states Jehoshaphat reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the name of Jehoshaphat's mother as recorded in 2 Chronicles 20:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Azubah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:31 identifies Jehoshaphat's mother as Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

questions.question: What was the reason given in 2 Chronicles 20:33 for the high places not being taken away during Jehoshaphat's reign?
options: The people had not prepared their hearts to God
The king commanded to keep them
They were protected by the priests
questions.correctAnswer: The people had not prepared their hearts to God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:33 explains the high places were not removed because the people had not prepared their hearts unto the God of their fathers.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'pazaz' in 2 Chronicles 20:27, translated as 'rejoice,' primarily mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To rejoice or be glad
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'pazaz' (פָּזַז) means to rejoice or be glad, which fits the context of 2 Chronicles 20:27 where the people rejoice over their enemies.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Chronicles 20:22-23 when the enemies destroy each other?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 20:22-23, irony is used as the enemies—children of Ammon and Moab—end up destroying each other rather than Judah doing so.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God fighting battles for His people as in 2 Chronicles 20:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:14
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:14 states, 'The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still,' directly echoing the message in 2 Chronicles 20:15 where the battle is God's, not theirs.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book also records the acts of Jehoshaphat as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 20:34?
options: The book of the kings of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The book of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:34 states the acts of Jehoshaphat are written in the book of Jehu son of Hanani, mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jehoshaphat's joyful return to Jerusalem in 2 Chronicles 20:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Gathering of spoils from enemies
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:25-26 describes the people gathering spoils and then blessing the LORD in the valley of Berachah, immediately preceding verse 27.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 20:32 characterize Jehoshaphat's religious conduct during his reign?
options: He walked in the way of Asa and did what was right in the LORD's sight
He abandoned the ways of his father
questions.correctAnswer: He walked in the way of Asa and did what was right in the LORD's sight
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:32 states Jehoshaphat walked in Asa's way and did right before the LORD, showing faithful conduct.

questions.question: What prophetic consequence is recorded in 2 Chronicles 20:37 for Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah?
options: The LORD broke his works and the ships were broken
He was blessed with abundant wealth
He was given victory in all battles
He was made king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD broke his works and the ships were broken
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:37 records Eliezer's prophecy that because Jehoshaphat joined with Ahaziah, the LORD broke his works and the ships were broken.

questions.question: What historical-cultural detail is revealed in 2 Chronicles 20:36 regarding Judah's naval ambitions?
options: They built ships at Eziongeber to go to Tarshish
They conquered the Philistines by sea
questions.correctAnswer: They built ships at Eziongeber to go to Tarshish
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:36 states Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah made ships at Eziongeber to go to Tarshish, indicating Judah's attempt at maritime trade.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 20:30, the realm of Jehoshaphat was in turmoil during his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:30 states the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet because his God gave him rest around about, indicating peace, not turmoil.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 20:6 teach about God's nature?
options: God is sovereign over all kingdoms and exercises supreme power and might
God is limited by earthly powers and requires human assistance
God is indifferent to the affairs of nations
God delegates power to human rulers exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign over all kingdoms and exercises supreme power and might
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:6 emphasizes God's sovereignty and omnipotence over all kingdoms and states that no one can withstand His power.

questions.question: What doctrine about prayer and intercession is taught in 2 Chronicles 20:9?
options: Prayer in God's house is an effective appeal to His mercy in times of judgment
Prayer is unnecessary because God acts independently of human requests
Only private prayer is acceptable to God
Intercession is only valid when accompanied by sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer in God's house is an effective appeal to His mercy in times of judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:9 shows that standing before God's house and crying out in affliction leads to God hearing and helping, highlighting the efficacy of corporate prayer in His presence.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine guidance and the Spirit is taught in 2 Chronicles 20:14?
options: The Spirit of the LORD inspires prophetic revelation in times of crisis
The Spirit only operates through dreams, never in public assembly
Divine guidance is given exclusively to kings, not Levites
The Spirit's presence guarantees immediate military victory
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the LORD inspires prophetic revelation in times of crisis
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:14 demonstrates that the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel to give a prophetic word of encouragement during a critical moment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 20:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 15 declares the battle is God's, not theirs, highlighting His sovereign control over the outcome.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 20:29 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear-inducing majesty
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 20:29 notes the fear of God fell on surrounding kingdoms when they heard the LORD fought against Israel's enemies, demonstrating His majestic and awe-inspiring presence.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 20 prepare for the New Testament theme of salvation by faith apart from works?
options: By showing that victory comes not by human effort but by trusting God's promise and standing still
By emphasizing the necessity of human military prowess for deliverance
By teaching that fasting and sacrifices alone secure salvation
By portraying reliance on prophetic signs to guarantee success
questions.correctAnswer: By showing that victory comes not by human effort but by trusting God's promise and standing still
questions.explanation: Verses like 20:17 teach that Judah should stand still and see God's salvation, prefiguring the doctrine of salvation by faith in God's power, not human works.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does 2 Chronicles 20:7-9 make with the Abrahamic covenant?
options: It affirms God's faithfulness to give the land to Abraham's descendants forever
It denies any ongoing covenant relationship with Israel
It shifts the promise from land to spiritual blessings exclusively
It portrays Israel as earning the land by military conquest alone
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's faithfulness to give the land to Abraham's descendants forever
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 recall God's covenant to Abraham to give the land to his seed and that the sanctuary is established there, underscoring covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 20 and 21 teach about faith and worship?
options: Faith in God and His prophets leads to established prosperity and is expressed through worship
Faith is irrelevant without military strength, and worship is optional
Worship replaces faith as the means to victory
Prosperity comes before faith and worship
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God and His prophets leads to established prosperity and is expressed through worship
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat commands belief in God and His prophets (v.20) and appoints singers to praise God (v.21), linking faith and worship to divine blessing.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 22 and 23 teach about divine justice and inter-enemy conflict?
options: God uses the enemies' own conflicts to bring about their judgment
God directly kills Israel's enemies without intermediary causes
Israel must fight and conquer enemies without divine intervention
Enemies unite to defeat Israel by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: God uses the enemies' own conflicts to bring about their judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 describe how the enemies fought among themselves under God's ambush, illustrating His use of enemy discord as judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 and 12 teach about human response to crisis and divine dependence?
options: Human fear leads to seeking the LORD in humility and dependence
Human strength alone is sufficient in crises
Distrust in God is justified when facing overwhelming odds
Seeking the LORD is a last resort after all else fails
questions.correctAnswer: Human fear leads to seeking the LORD in humility and dependence
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat's fear (v.3) prompts a fast and seeking God (v.12), showing that acknowledgement of human weakness leads to dependence on God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 20:22-24 teaches that God causes death arbitrarily. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God orchestrates victory by causing enemy self-destruction as judgment, not arbitrary death
God randomly kills people without purpose
God punishes all enemies equally regardless of their actions
God's victory is a result of human military strategy alone
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates victory by causing enemy self-destruction as judgment, not arbitrary death
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show God setting ambushes so enemies fight one another, indicating purposeful divine judgment, not arbitrary death.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant faithfulness is demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 20:10?
options: God's past restraint in judgment shows His covenant mercy despite Israel not fully obeying
God is unfaithful to His promises
God punishes Israel immediately for every failure
God ignores the surrounding nations completely
questions.correctAnswer: God's past restraint in judgment shows His covenant mercy despite Israel not fully obeying
questions.explanation: Verse 10 recalls God not allowing Israel to invade certain peoples, indicating His mercy and covenant faithfulness even when Israel did not fully obey.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by Jehoshaphat's response in 2 Chronicles 20:18?
options: God's worthiness of worship and reverence
questions.correctAnswer: God's worthiness of worship and reverence
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat and the people bow and worship in 20:18, indicating God's worthiness and holiness that demands reverence.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does 2 Chronicles 20:26 develop?
options: The practice of blessing God publicly in response to His deliverance
The rejection of God after victory
The idea that victory requires isolation from God
The establishment of a new covenant replacing the old
questions.correctAnswer: The practice of blessing God publicly in response to His deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 26 describes assembling in the valley of Berachah to bless the LORD, affirming public thanksgiving as a response to salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 35 and 37 teach about the dangers of ungodly alliances?
options: Joining with wicked partners leads to divine judgment and failure of plans
All political alliances are blessed by God
God ignores human alliances in history
Wicked alliances guarantee success by worldly means
questions.correctAnswer: Joining with wicked partners leads to divine judgment and failure of plans
questions.explanation: Verses 35-37 recount Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah, which results in the breaking of ships by God's judgment through prophecy.
